title: Most people think courage is loud.
paragraphs: Most people think courage is loud.
They imagine speeches, crowds, applause, and recognition.
But the Bible shows us something different.
After Jesus died, many of His followers were hiding. Fear filled the streets of Jerusalem. The same leaders who condemned Jesus still held power, and anyone associated with Him could lose everything.
Then a man stepped forward.

Not a fisherman.
Not one of the twelve disciples.
A respected council member.
Joseph of Arimathea.
The same council that condemned Jesus… Joseph was part of it.
And yet when the moment came, he did something dangerous.
He went directly to Pilate and asked for the body of Jesus.
That request publicly revealed where he stood.

His reputation.
His position.
His safety.
All of it was suddenly on the line.
But Joseph understood something many people forget:
Real courage is not always loud.

Sometimes courage is quiet.
Sometimes it is a single decision made when no one is cheering.
Sometimes it is doing what is right when silence would be safer.
Joseph didn’t preach a sermon that day.
He simply honored Jesus when others stayed hidden.
History remembers the loud heroes.
But heaven also remembers the quiet ones.
And sometimes the most powerful act of faith is simply this:
Stepping forward when it matters.

History remembers the loud heroes.
But heaven also remembers the quiet ones.
